claim: Recurrent connections are thought to be a common feature of the neural circuits that encode memories.
source: Recurrent connections are thought to be a common feature of the neural circuits that encode memories, but how memories are laid down in such circuits is not fully understood.
evidence: This is a statement about established scientific thinking in the field.

claim: Courtship memory in Drosophila relies on the recurrent circuit between mushroom body gamma (MBγ), M6 output, and aSP13 dopaminergic neurons.
source: Here we present evidence that courtship memory in Drosophila relies on the recurrent circuit between mushroom body gamma (MBγ), M6 output, and aSP13 dopaminergic neurons.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by multiple experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: aSP13 neurons exhibit persistent neuronal activity.
source: We demonstrate persistent neuronal activity of aSP13 neurons and show that it transiently potentiates synaptic transmission from MBγ>M6 neurons.
evidence: This is demonstrated through calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: Persistent aSP13 activity transiently potentiates synaptic transmission from MBγ to M6 neurons.
source: We demonstrate persistent neuronal activity of aSP13 neurons and show that it transiently potentiates synaptic transmission from MBγ>M6 neurons.
evidence: This is supported by optogenetic and calcium imaging experiments shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: M6 neurons provide input to aSP13 neurons.
source: M6 neurons in turn provide input to aSP13 neurons, prolonging potentiation of MBγ>M6 synapses over time periods that match short-term memory.
evidence: This is demonstrated by calcium imaging showing aSP13 response to M6 activation in Figure 4.

claim: M6 input to aSP13 neurons prolongs potentiation of MBγ>M6 synapses over time periods that match short-term memory.
source: M6 neurons in turn provide input to aSP13 neurons, prolonging potentiation of MBγ>M6 synapses over time periods that match short-term memory.
evidence: This is supported by the time course experiments in Figure 3D showing potentiation lasting 2-3 hours.

claim: Working memory is thought to reflect persistent activity generated within neural networks, including recurrent circuits.
source: Working memory is thought to reflect persistent activity generated within neural networks, including recurrent circuits (Wang, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wang, 2001.

claim: Short-term memory (STM) and long-term memory (LTM) involve changes in synaptic efficacy due to functional and structural modification of synaptic connections.
source: In contrast, short-term memory (STM) and long-term memory (LTM) involves changes in synaptic efficacy due to functional and structural modification of synaptic connections (Kandel, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kandel, 2001.

claim: Courtship memory in Drosophila can last from minutes to days, depending on the duration and intensity of training.
source: A robust form of memory in Drosophila is courtship memory, which can last from minutes to days, depending on the duration and intensity of training (Siegel and Hall, 1979; McBride et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Siegel and Hall, 1979 and McBride et al., 1999.

claim: Naïve Drosophila males eagerly court both virgin females and mated females.
source: Naïve Drosophila males eagerly court both virgin females, which are generally receptive, and mated females, which are not (Manning, 1967; Wolfner, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Manning, 1967 and Wolfner, 2003.

claim: Virgin females are generally receptive to male courtship.
source: Naïve Drosophila males eagerly court both virgin females, which are generally receptive, and mated females, which are not (Manning, 1967; Wolfner, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Manning, 1967 and Wolfner, 2003.

claim: Mated females are not receptive to male courtship.
source: Naïve Drosophila males eagerly court both virgin females, which are generally receptive, and mated females, which are not (Manning, 1967; Wolfner, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Manning, 1967 and Wolfner, 2003.

claim: Upon rejection by mated females, males become subsequently less likely to court other mated females.
source: However, upon rejection by mated females, they become subsequently less likely to court other mated females (Tompkins, 1984).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tompkins, 1984.

claim: Courtship conditioning is the selective suppression of courtship towards mated females.
source: This selective suppression of courtship towards mated females, called courtship conditioning, can be attributed to the enhanced sensitivity of experienced males to an inhibitory male pheromone deposited on the female during mating, cis-vaccenyl acetate (cVA) (Keleman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a definition provided in the text with citation support.

claim: Courtship conditioning can be attributed to the enhanced sensitivity of experienced males to cis-vaccenyl acetate (cVA).
source: This selective suppression of courtship towards mated females, called courtship conditioning, can be attributed to the enhanced sensitivity of experienced males to an inhibitory male pheromone deposited on the female during mating, cis-vaccenyl acetate (cVA) (Keleman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Keleman et al., 2012.

claim: cVA is an inhibitory male pheromone deposited on the female during mating.
source: This selective suppression of courtship towards mated females, called courtship conditioning, can be attributed to the enhanced sensitivity of experienced males to an inhibitory male pheromone deposited on the female during mating, cis-vaccenyl acetate (cVA) (Keleman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Keleman et al., 2012.

claim: Olfactory memory in insects relies on the function of the mushroom body (MB).
source: Olfactory memory in insects relies on the function of a central brain structure called the mushroom body (MB) (de Belle and Heisenberg, 1994; Heisenberg et al., 1985).
evidence: This is supported by citations to de Belle and Heisenberg, 1994 and Heisenberg et al., 1985.

claim: The principal MB cells are the cholinergic Kenyon cells (KCs).
source: The principal MB cells, the cholinergic Kenyon cells (KCs) (Barnstedt et al., 2016), receive input from sensory pathways in the dendritic calyx region and from dopaminergic neurons (DANs) in the axonal lobes of the MB.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Barnstedt et al., 2016.

claim: Kenyon cells receive input from sensory pathways in the dendritic calyx region.
source: The principal MB cells, the cholinergic Kenyon cells (KCs) (Barnstedt et al., 2016), receive input from sensory pathways in the dendritic calyx region and from dopaminergic neurons (DANs) in the axonal lobes of the MB.
evidence: This is a statement about established anatomical connectivity.

claim: Kenyon cells receive input from dopaminergic neurons (DANs) in the axonal lobes of the MB.
source: The principal MB cells, the cholinergic Kenyon cells (KCs) (Barnstedt et al., 2016), receive input from sensory pathways in the dendritic calyx region and from dopaminergic neurons (DANs) in the axonal lobes of the MB.
evidence: This is a statement about established anatomical connectivity.

claim: MB lobes are compartmentalized, with each compartment innervated by specific classes of DANs and MB output neurons (MBONs).
source: These MB lobes are compartmentalized, with each compartment innervated by specific classes of DANs and MB output neurons (MBONs) (Aso et al., 2014a; Mao and Davis, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Aso et al., 2014a and Mao and Davis, 2009.

claim: MBONs receive input from both KCs and DANs.
source: MBONs receive input from both KCs and DANs (Takemura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Takemura et al., 2017.

claim: Short-term courtship conditioning is mediated by the aSP13 class of DANs.
source: We previously established that short-term courtship conditioning is mediated by the aSP13 class of DANs (also known as the PAM-γ5 neurons, [Aso et al., 2014a]), which innervate the MBγ5 compartment.
evidence: This is a reference to previous work by the authors.

claim: aSP13 neurons are also known as PAM-γ5 neurons.
source: We previously established that short-term courtship conditioning is mediated by the aSP13 class of DANs (also known as the PAM-γ5 neurons, [Aso et al., 2014a]), which innervate the MBγ5 compartment.
evidence: This is a nomenclature clarification with citation support.

claim: aSP13 neurons innervate the MBγ5 compartment.
source: We previously established that short-term courtship conditioning is mediated by the aSP13 class of DANs (also known as the PAM-γ5 neurons, [Aso et al., 2014a]), which innervate the MBγ5 compartment.
evidence: This is an anatomical fact supported by citation.

claim: The activity of aSP13 neurons is essential for courtship conditioning in experienced males.
source: The activity of aSP13 neurons is essential for courtship conditioning in experienced males and sufficient to induce conditioning in naïve males (Keleman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Keleman et al., 2012.

claim: The activity of aSP13 neurons is sufficient to induce conditioning in naïve males.
source: The activity of aSP13 neurons is essential for courtship conditioning in experienced males and sufficient to induce conditioning in naïve males (Keleman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Keleman et al., 2012.

claim: Courtship memory requires the corresponding MBγ KCs.
source: Here we demonstrate that courtship memory also requires the corresponding MBγ KCs and the MBγ5 MBONs, the glutamatergic M6 neurons (also known as MBON-γ5β'2a neurons [Aso et al., 2014a]).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the behavioral experiments in Figure 1A.

claim: Courtship memory requires the MBγ5 MBONs, the glutamatergic M6 neurons.
source: Here we demonstrate that courtship memory also requires the corresponding MBγ KCs and the MBγ5 MBONs, the glutamatergic M6 neurons (also known as MBON-γ5β'2a neurons [Aso et al., 2014a]).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the behavioral experiments in Figure 1B.

claim: M6 neurons are also known as MBON-γ5β'2a neurons.
source: Here we demonstrate that courtship memory also requires the corresponding MBγ KCs and the MBγ5 MBONs, the glutamatergic M6 neurons (also known as MBON-γ5β'2a neurons [Aso et al., 2014a]).
evidence: This is a nomenclature clarification with citation support.

claim: MBγ, M6, and aSP13 neurons form a recurrent circuit.
source: Furthermore, we present evidence that MBγ, M6, and aSP13 neurons form a recurrent circuit and that persistent activity of the aSP13 neurons mediates plasticity at the MBγ to M6 synapses that can last from minutes to hours.
evidence: This is supported by the connectivity and functional experiments shown in Figures 2-4.

claim: Persistent activity of aSP13 neurons mediates plasticity at the MBγ to M6 synapses that can last from minutes to hours.
source: Furthermore, we present evidence that MBγ, M6, and aSP13 neurons form a recurrent circuit and that persistent activity of the aSP13 neurons mediates plasticity at the MBγ to M6 synapses that can last from minutes to hours.
evidence: This is supported by the time course experiments in Figure 3D.

claim: M6 activity is required for memory readout.
source: Consistent with this model, M6 activity is required not only for memory readout but also, like aSP13, for memory formation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the behavioral experiments in Figure 4I.

claim: M6 activity is required for memory formation.
source: Consistent with this model, M6 activity is required not only for memory readout but also, like aSP13, for memory formation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the behavioral experiments in Figure 4I.

claim: Persistent aSP13 activity within the MBγ>M6>aSP13 recurrent circuit lays the foundation for short-term courtship memory.
source: These data support a model in which persistent aSP13 activity within the MBγ>M6>aSP13 recurrent circuit lays the foundation for short-term courtship memory.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, based on the integration of all experimental results.

claim: Control flies expressing inactive tetanus toxin (UAS-TNTQ) typically show a suppression index of ~40–50%.
source: Control flies expressing an inactive form of tetanus toxin (UAS-TNTQ) typically showed a SI of ~40–50% (Figure 1A,B; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and shown in Figures 1A and 1B.

claim: Males in which M6 neurons or MBγ neurons were silenced with tetanus toxin showed much less or no suppression.
source: By contrast, males in which M6 neurons or MBγ neurons were silenced with an inhibitory form of tetanus toxin (UAS-TNT) showed much less or no suppression (Figure 1A,B; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and shown in Figures 1A and 1B.

claim: DAN inputs to a given MB compartment are believed to modulate synaptic transmission from MB neurons to MBONs, primarily through their presynaptic inputs onto the KCs.
source: The DAN inputs to a given MB compartment are believed to modulate synaptic transmission from MB neurons to MBONs, primarily through their presynaptic inputs onto the KCs (Kim et al., 2007; Qin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2007 and Qin et al., 2012.

claim: Some studies have indicated that DANs enhance KC>MBON transmission.
source: Some studies have indicated that DANs enhance KC>MBON transmission (Cohn et al., 2015; Owald et al., 2015; Plaçais et al., 2013; Pai et al., 2013), whereas others have suggested that DANs depress these synapses (Aso et al., 2014a; Hige et al., 2015; Owald et al., 2015; Séjourné et al., 2011; Hattori et al., 2017; Lewis et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Some studies have suggested that DANs depress KC>MBON synapses.
source: Some studies have indicated that DANs enhance KC>MBON transmission (Cohn et al., 2015; Owald et al., 2015; Plaçais et al., 2013; Pai et al., 2013), whereas others have suggested that DANs depress these synapses (Aso et al., 2014a; Hige et al., 2015; Owald et al., 2015; Séjourné et al., 2011; Hattori et al., 2017; Lewis et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The sign of DAN modulation of KC>MBON transmission may depend upon the context.
source: The sign of modulation may therefore depend upon the context.
evidence: This is an inference based on the conflicting results from different studies.

claim: Artificial activation of M6 suppresses courtship.
source: We predicted that, if M6 is the relevant MBON for courtship conditioning, then artificial activation of M6 should suppress courtship.
evidence: This prediction is confirmed by the data in Figure 1D.

claim: M6 activation suppresses male courtship with equal potency in both naïve and experienced males.
source: By contrast, M6 activation suppressed male courtship with equal potency in both naïve and experienced males (Figure 1D; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: MBγ activation is significantly more potent in experienced males than in naïve males.
source: We found that MBγ activation was significantly more potent in experienced males than in naïve males, in which it had only a small effect on courtship (Figure 1C; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: MBγ activation has only a small effect on courtship in naïve males.
source: We found that MBγ activation was significantly more potent in experienced males than in naïve males, in which it had only a small effect on courtship (Figure 1C; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Courtship experience with mated females potentiates synaptic transmission from MBγ to M6 cells.
source: We conclude from these data that courtship experience with mated females potentiates synaptic transmission from MBγ to M6 cells.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the differential effects of MBγ activation in naïve vs. experienced males shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Cholinergic synaptic transmission from MBγ to M6 cells is initially weak but can be acutely potentiated by dopamine.
source: Together, these data indicate that cholinergic synaptic transmission from MBγ to M6 cells is initially weak but can be acutely potentiated by dopamine.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experiments in Figure 2 showing that M6 response to MBγ activation requires dopamine.

claim: A strong dose-dependent calcium response was consistently observed in M6 neurons in trials with dopamine during the SFOCatCh ON period.
source: However, a strong dose-dependent calcium response was consistently observed in trials with dopamine during the SFOCatCh ON period.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B-D.

claim: Little or no calcium response was observed in M6 neurons during the SFOCatCh OFF periods.
source: In contrast, little or no response was observed during either the SFOCatCh OFF periods (Figure 2B–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2) or the SFOCatCh ON period after dopamine washout (Figure 2B,C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B-D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Little or no calcium response was observed in M6 neurons during the SFOCatCh ON period after dopamine washout.
source: In contrast, little or no response was observed during either the SFOCatCh OFF periods (Figure 2B–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2) or the SFOCatCh ON period after dopamine washout (Figure 2B,C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B-C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The response of M6 to dopamine and SFOCatCh was completely abolished by application of the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor antagonist mecamylamine.
source: The response to dopamine and SFOCatCh was completely abolished by application of the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor antagonist mecamylamine (Figure 2F), which blocks synaptic transmission from KCs to MBONs (Barnstedt et al., 2016).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Mecamylamine blocks synaptic transmission from KCs to MBONs.
source: The response to dopamine and SFOCatCh was completely abolished by application of the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor antagonist mecamylamine (Figure 2F), which blocks synaptic transmission from KCs to MBONs (Barnstedt et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Barnstedt et al., 2016.

claim: After 3–4 trials of repetitive MBγ stimulation, a significant calcium response was observed in M6 neurons.
source: However, after 3–4 trials a significant calcium response was observed (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: The M6 calcium response increased upon each successive stimulation before reaching a plateau after approximately 20 trials.
source: This response increased upon each successive stimulation before reaching a plateau after approximately 20 trials.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The M6 response to repetitive MBγ stimulation was blocked by the dopamine D1-type receptor antagonist SCH23390.
source: This response was blocked by the dopamine D1-type receptor antagonist SCH23390 (Figure 3C), regardless of whether it was applied during the induction or plateau phase.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Upon repetitive stimulation of MBγ neurons, endogenous dopamine enables synaptic transmission to M6 neurons.
source: This suggests that, upon repetitive stimulation of MBγ neurons, endogenous dopamine enables synaptic transmission to M6 neurons.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that the response is blocked by a dopamine receptor antagonist.

claim: The most likely source of endogenous dopamine supply is the aSP13 neurons.
source: The most likely source of this endogenous dopamine supply is the aSP13 neurons.
evidence: This is inferred from the anatomical connectivity and the fact that aSP13 neurons are dopaminergic and innervate the same compartment.

claim: aSP13 DANs respond in a similar manner as M6 to the repetitive activation of MBγ neurons.
source: Indeed, by shifting GCaMP6s from M6 to aSP13, we confirmed that the aSP13 DANs respond in a similar manner as M6 to the repetitive activation of MBγ neurons (Figure 3E,F)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3E and 3F.

claim: Potentiation at MBγ>M6 synapses was barely diminished after 1 hr.
source: Potentiation at MBγ>M6 synapses was barely diminished after 1 hr, but fell to about 50% of its initial level after 3 hr (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Potentiation at MBγ>M6 synapses fell to about 50% of its initial level after 3 hr.
source: Potentiation at MBγ>M6 synapses was barely diminished after 1 hr, but fell to about 50% of its initial level after 3 hr (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The persistence of potentiation at MBγ>M6 synapses is in line with the persistence of the courtship memory after a 30 min training period.
source: The persistence of potentiation at MBγ>M6 synapses in these experiments is thus in line with the persistence of the courtship memory after a 30 min training period (Keleman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison between the physiological and behavioral timescales, with citation support.

claim: DANs and MBONs innervating the same MB compartment have the potential to form recurrent loops, with MBONs providing input to DANs.
source: Anatomically, DANs and MBONs innervating the same MB compartment, have the potential to form recurrent loops, with MBONs providing input to DANs (Aso et al., 2014a; Takemura et al., 2017; Ichinose et al., 2015; Eichler et al., 2017; Owald et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The axonal termini of M6 MBONs are closely apposed to the aSP13 dendrites.
source: In particular, the axonal termini of M6 MBONs are closely apposed to the aSP13 dendrites (Aso et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Aso et al., 2014a.

claim: Acute activation of M6 neurons produces a strong calcium response in aSP13.
source: Indeed, acute activation of M6 neurons produced a strong calcium response in aSP13 (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: The aSP13 response to M6 activation was blocked by the NMDA receptor antagonist AP-5.
source: This response was blocked by the NMDA receptor antagonist AP-5 (Figure 4C), consistent with glutamatergic transmission from M6 cells.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The aSP13 response to M6 activation is consistent with glutamatergic transmission from M6 cells.
source: This response was blocked by the NMDA receptor antagonist AP-5 (Figure 4C), consistent with glutamatergic transmission from M6 cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that the response is blocked by an NMDA receptor antagonist.

claim: Activation of MBγ neurons with SFOCatCh elicits a strong calcium response in aSP13 neurons.
source: Activation of MBγ neurons with SFOCatCh also elicited a strong calcium response in aSP13 neurons (Figure 4E,F) that was also dependent on glutamatergic neurotransmission, as well as both cholinergic transmission and dopamine (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4E and 4F.

claim: The aSP13 response to MBγ activation is dependent on glutamatergic neurotransmission.
source: Activation of MBγ neurons with SFOCatCh also elicited a strong calcium response in aSP13 neurons (Figure 4E,F) that was also dependent on glutamatergic neurotransmission, as well as both cholinergic transmission and dopamine (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The aSP13 response to MBγ activation is dependent on cholinergic transmission.
source: Activation of MBγ neurons with SFOCatCh also elicited a strong calcium response in aSP13 neurons (Figure 4E,F) that was also dependent on glutamatergic neurotransmission, as well as both cholinergic transmission and dopamine (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The aSP13 response to MBγ activation is dependent on dopamine.
source: Activation of MBγ neurons with SFOCatCh also elicited a strong calcium response in aSP13 neurons (Figure 4E,F) that was also dependent on glutamatergic neurotransmission, as well as both cholinergic transmission and dopamine (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The calcium response in aSP13 neurons to M6 activation persists into the post-stimulus SFOCatCh OFF period.
source: Whereas the M6 response to MBγ activation was diminished in the post-stimulus OFF period in trials with dopamine (Figure 2B,C), the response of aSP13 neurons to either M6 or MBγ activation persisted into the post-stimulus SFOCatCh OFF period (Figure 4A,B,E and F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A, B, E, and F.

claim: The calcium response in aSP13 neurons to MBγ activation persists into the post-stimulus SFOCatCh OFF period.
source: Whereas the M6 response to MBγ activation was diminished in the post-stimulus OFF period in trials with dopamine (Figure 2B,C), the response of aSP13 neurons to either M6 or MBγ activation persisted into the post-stimulus SFOCatCh OFF period (Figure 4A,B,E and F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A, B, E, and F.

claim: The calcium response in aSP13 gradually declines over a 2 min period after M6 or MBγ activation.
source: In each case, the calcium response in aSP13 gradually declined over a 2 min period (Figure 4D and H).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4D and 4H.

claim: The persistent response of aSP13 neurons is not an intrinsic property of aSP13 neurons.
source: The persistent response of aSP13 neurons is not an intrinsic property of aSP13 neurons, since it was not observed when SFOCatCh was used to activate the aSP13 neurons themselves (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The persistent activity of aSP13 is induced by glutamatergic transmission from M6 cells.
source: Given that the response of aSP13 to MBγ or M6 activation is blocked by AP-5, we infer that this persistent activity is induced by glutamatergic transmission from M6 cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that the response is blocked by an NMDA receptor antagonist.

claim: Activity of aSP13 neurons is strictly required during the training period of courtship conditioning.
source: Activity of aSP13 neurons is strictly required during the training period of courtship conditioning (Keleman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Keleman et al., 2012.

claim: Synaptic transmission from aSP13 is only required during memory acquisition.
source: Thus, whereas synaptic transmission from aSP13 is only required during memory acquisition (Keleman et al., 2012), M6 output is required during both acquisition and recall (Figure 4I; Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Keleman et al., 2012.

claim: M6 output is required during both memory acquisition and recall.
source: Thus, whereas synaptic transmission from aSP13 is only required during memory acquisition (Keleman et al., 2012), M6 output is required during both acquisition and recall (Figure 4I; Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Males in which M6 neurotransmission was blocked during training had suppression indices indistinguishable from 0.
source: Males in which M6 neurotransmission was blocked either during training or during testing had suppression indices indistinguishable from 0.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Males in which M6 neurotransmission was blocked during testing had suppression indices indistinguishable from 0.
source: Males in which M6 neurotransmission was blocked either during training or during testing had suppression indices indistinguishable from 0.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4I.

claim: STM formation requires the MBγ>M6>aSP13 recurrent circuit.
source: We therefore propose that STM formation requires the MBγ>M6>aSP13 recurrent circuit, whereas readout occurs through other M6-dependent pathways.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the integration of behavioral and physiological data.

claim: Memory readout occurs through M6-dependent pathways that do not involve aSP13.
source: We therefore propose that STM formation requires the MBγ>M6>aSP13 recurrent circuit, whereas readout occurs through other M6-dependent pathways.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that M6 is required for both acquisition and recall, while aSP13 is only required for acquisition.

claim: When a naïve male courts a mated female, the aSP13 and MBγ neurons may both be activated.
source: When a naïve male courts a mated female, the aSP13 and MBγ neurons may both be activated, perhaps in response to behavioral rejection and olfactory stimuli presented by the female, respectively.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the natural activation of these neurons during courtship.

claim: Dopamine released by aSP13 neurons potentiates transmission from MBγ to M6 neurons.
source: Dopamine released by aSP13 neurons potentiates transmission from MBγ to M6 neurons, which in turn provide a recurrent excitatory glutamatergic input back onto aSP13 neurons.
evidence: This is supported by the experiments in Figures 2-4.

claim: M6 neurons provide a recurrent excitatory glutamatergic input back onto aSP13 neurons.
source: Dopamine released by aSP13 neurons potentiates transmission from MBγ to M6 neurons, which in turn provide a recurrent excitatory glutamatergic input back onto aSP13 neurons.
evidence: This is supported by the experiments in Figure 4.

claim: Upon activation by M6, aSP13 activity persists for several minutes.
source: Upon activation by M6, aSP13 activity persists for several minutes, providing a short time window during which continued MBγ activity can further drive M6 and aSP13.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4D and 4H.

claim: Sustained aSP13 activity can lead to a longer-lasting accumulation of dopamine in the γ5 compartment.
source: Thus sustained, aSP13 activity can lead to a longer-lasting accumulation of dopamine in the γ5 compartment, facilitating MBγ>M6 neurotransmission for up to 2–3 hr.
evidence: This is inferred from the persistent activity of aSP13 and the time course of potentiation.

claim: Sustained aSP13 activity facilitates MBγ>M6 neurotransmission for up to 2–3 hr.
source: Thus sustained, aSP13 activity can lead to a longer-lasting accumulation of dopamine in the γ5 compartment, facilitating MBγ>M6 neurotransmission for up to 2–3 hr.
evidence: This is supported by the time course experiments in Figure 3D.

claim: The timescales for physiological processes in ex vivo brain preparations broadly match the dynamics of courtship training and short-term memory formation.
source: The timescales for these physiological processes in ex vivo brain preparations broadly match the dynamics of courtship training and short-term memory formation.
evidence: This is a comparison between the physiological and behavioral timescales.

claim: In the standard training paradigm, the male typically courts the female over several minutes.
source: In our standard training paradigm, the male typically courts the female over several minutes, during which he performs a series of courtship bouts, each lasting for several seconds.
evidence: This is a description of the behavioral paradigm used in the study.

claim: During courtship training, the male performs a series of courtship bouts, each lasting for several seconds.
source: In our standard training paradigm, the male typically courts the female over several minutes, during which he performs a series of courtship bouts, each lasting for several seconds.
evidence: This is a description of the behavioral paradigm used in the study.

claim: Courtship training results in a behavioral memory that lasts for several hours.
source: As a result, a behavioral memory forms that lasts for several hours (Keleman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Keleman et al., 2012.

claim: Memory formation during training requires both M6 and aSP13.
source: Memory formation during training requires both M6 and aSP13, consistent with the notion that it reflects activation of the recurrent circuit (Figure 4 and [Keleman et al., 2012]).
evidence: This is supported by the behavioral experiments in Figure 4I and citation to Keleman et al., 2012.

claim: Memory readout requires M6 but not aSP13.
source: Memory readout requires M6 but not aSP13 (Figure 4 and [Keleman et al., 2012]), and so evidently does not involve the recurrent circuit.
evidence: This is supported by the behavioral experiments in Figure 4I and citation to Keleman et al., 2012.

claim: Memory readout does not involve the recurrent circuit.
source: Memory readout requires M6 but not aSP13 (Figure 4 and [Keleman et al., 2012]), and so evidently does not involve the recurrent circuit.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that aSP13 is not required for memory readout.

claim: M6 suppresses courtship through aSP13-independent pathways.
source: We infer that M6 suppresses courtship through other, aSP13-independent, pathways, and that its ability to do so is independent of experience.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that M6 activation suppresses courtship equally in naïve and experienced males.

claim: M6's ability to suppress courtship is independent of experience.
source: We infer that M6 suppresses courtship through other, aSP13-independent, pathways, and that its ability to do so is independent of experience.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that M6 activation suppresses courtship equally in naïve and experienced males.

claim: The consequence of training is to provide MBγ neurons with access to the M6-dependent courtship suppression pathway.
source: The consequence of training is to provide MBγ neurons with access to this M6-dependent courtship suppression pathway (Figure 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of MBγ activation in naïve vs. experienced males shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Persistent aSP13 activity is evidently not an intrinsic property of aSP13.
source: The persistent response in aSP13 is evidently not an intrinsic property of aSP13, as it is not induced when aSP13 neurons themselves are activated.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Persistent aSP13 activity is induced in response to transient M6 activation.
source: Persistent aSP13 activity is induced in response to transient M6 activation, and is not associated with any persistent activity of M6 neurons themselves.
evidence: This is shown in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: Persistent aSP13 activity is not associated with any persistent activity of M6 neurons themselves.
source: Persistent aSP13 activity is induced in response to transient M6 activation, and is not associated with any persistent activity of M6 neurons themselves.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2.

claim: Persistent aSP13 activity may reflect unusually prolonged activation of the glutamatergic M6>aSP13 synapses.
source: One possibility is that aSP13 persistence reflects unusually prolonged activation of the glutamatergic M6 >aSP13 synapses, or perhaps lies within interposed but still unidentified circuit elements.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism underlying persistent aSP13 activity.

claim: Persistent aSP13 activity may lie within interposed but still unidentified circuit elements.
source: One possibility is that aSP13 persistence reflects unusually prolonged activation of the glutamatergic M6 >aSP13 synapses, or perhaps lies within interposed but still unidentified circuit elements.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism underlying persistent aSP13 activity.

claim: M6 neurons activate a courtship suppression pathway.
source: Given that M6 neurons activate a courtship suppression pathway, the potentiation of MBγ>M6 neurotransmission may explain why MBγ activation suppresses courtship in trained but not naïve flies.
evidence: This is inferred from the behavioral experiments in Figure 1D.

claim: The potentiation of MBγ>M6 neurotransmission may explain why MBγ activation suppresses courtship in trained but not naïve flies.
source: Given that M6 neurons activate a courtship suppression pathway, the potentiation of MBγ>M6 neurotransmission may explain why MBγ activation suppresses courtship in trained but not naïve flies.
evidence: This is inferred from the behavioral experiments in Figure 1C.

claim: MBγ neurons likely do not specifically respond to cVA.
source: But MBγ neurons likely do not specifically respond to cVA (Caron et al., 2013; Gruntman and Turner, 2013), so this change alone cannot account for the enhanced sensitivity of trained flies to cVA.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Caron et al., 2013 and Gruntman and Turner, 2013.

claim: A small and variable subset of MB γ neurons do receive input from the olfactory pathway that processes cVA.
source: A small and variable subset of MB γneurons do receive input from the olfactory pathway that processes cVA, but cVA is not required during training (Keleman et al., 2012) and it is difficult to envision any other mechanism by which aSP13-dependent plasticity could be specifically restricted to the cVA-responsive MBγ neurons.
evidence: This is a statement about the connectivity of MBγ neurons.

claim: cVA is not required during training.
source: A small and variable subset of MB γneurons do receive input from the olfactory pathway that processes cVA, but cVA is not required during training (Keleman et al., 2012) and it is difficult to envision any other mechanism by which aSP13-dependent plasticity could be specifically restricted to the cVA-responsive MBγ neurons.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Keleman et al., 2012.

claim: M6 neurons encode a generic aversive signal.
source: Alternatively, it has been suggested that M6 neurons encode a generic aversive signal (Aso et al., 2014b), and so specificity to cVA might instead arise in downstream circuits that selectively integrate M6 output with the innate cVA-processing pathway from the lateral horn.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Aso et al., 2014b.

claim: Other MBONs have been implicated in courtship learning.
source: In this regard, it is interesting to note that other MBONs have been implicated in courtship learning (Montague and Baker, 2016) or general aversion (Aso et al., 2014b), but M6 is the only MBON common to both.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Montague and Baker, 2016.

claim: Other MBONs have been implicated in general aversion.
source: In this regard, it is interesting to note that other MBONs have been implicated in courtship learning (Montague and Baker, 2016) or general aversion (Aso et al., 2014b), but M6 is the only MBON common to both.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Aso et al., 2014b.

claim: M6 is the only MBON common to both courtship learning and general aversion.
source: In this regard, it is interesting to note that other MBONs have been implicated in courtship learning (Montague and Baker, 2016) or general aversion (Aso et al., 2014b), but M6 is the only MBON common to both.
evidence: This is inferred from the citations to Montague and Baker, 2016 and Aso et al., 2014b.

claim: Late activation of aSP13 neurons in the time window of 8–10 hr after training is both necessary and sufficient to consolidate STM to LTM.
source: Late activation of the same aSP13 neurons in the time window of 8–10 hr after training is both necessary and sufficient to consolidate STM to LTM (Krüttner et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Krüttner et al., 2015.

claim: In the time window when STM would otherwise decay, reactivation of the MBγ>M6>aSP13 recurrent circuit may consolidate it into LTM.
source: Thus, in the time window when STM would otherwise decay (Keleman et al., 2007), reactivation of the same MBγ>M6>aSP13 recurrent circuit may instead consolidate it into LTM.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the integration of findings from this study and previous work.

claim: The mechanism by which aSP13 neurons are reactivated for LTM consolidation is unknown.
source: The mechanism by which aSP13 neurons are reactivated is unknown, but is evidently dependent upon their activation within the MBγ>M6>aSP13 recurrent circuit during training.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: aSP13 reactivation for LTM consolidation is dependent upon their activation within the MBγ>M6>aSP13 recurrent circuit during training.
source: The mechanism by which aSP13 neurons are reactivated is unknown, but is evidently dependent upon their activation within the MBγ>M6>aSP13 recurrent circuit during training.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement for aSP13 activity during training.

claim: Brief persistent activity of aSP13 neurons represents a neural correlate of courtship working memory.
source: In summary, our data suggest that a brief persistent activity of aSP13 neurons represents a neural correlate of courtship working memory, while the prolonged potentiation of MBγ>M6 synapses corresponds to STM.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the integration of all experimental results.

claim: Prolonged potentiation of MBγ>M6 synapses corresponds to STM.
source: In summary, our data suggest that a brief persistent activity of aSP13 neurons represents a neural correlate of courtship working memory, while the prolonged potentiation of MBγ>M6 synapses corresponds to STM.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the integration of all experimental results.

claim: Persistent activity of the dopaminergic neurons in the MBγ>M6>aSP13 feedback loop lays the foundation for formation of short-term courtship memory in Drosophila.
source: We propose that persistent activity of the dopaminergic neurons in the MBγ>M6>aSP13 feedback loop lays the foundation for formation of short-term courtship memory in Drosophila, and that later reactivation of the same recurrent circuit consolidates STM into LTM.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, based on the integration of all experimental results.

claim: Later reactivation of the MBγ>M6>aSP13 recurrent circuit consolidates STM into LTM.
source: We propose that persistent activity of the dopaminergic neurons in the MBγ>M6>aSP13 feedback loop lays the foundation for formation of short-term courtship memory in Drosophila, and that later reactivation of the same recurrent circuit consolidates STM into LTM.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the integration of findings from this study and previous work on LTM consolidation.

claim: The prevailing view of memory progression in the Drosophila MB is that distinct memory phases are located in different compartments or lobes.
source: Thus, in contrast to the prevailing view of memory progression in the Drosophila MB that distinct memory phases are located in different compartments or lobes (Aso and Rubin, 2016; Davis, 2011; Pascual and Préat, 2001), our data suggest that in the context of courtship conditioning, working memory, STM, and LTM all reside in the same γ5 compartment.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Aso and Rubin, 2016; Davis, 2011; and Pascual and Préat, 2001.

claim: In the context of courtship conditioning, working memory, STM, and LTM all reside in the same γ5 compartment.
source: Thus, in contrast to the prevailing view of memory progression in the Drosophila MB that distinct memory phases are located in different compartments or lobes (Aso and Rubin, 2016; Davis, 2011; Pascual and Préat, 2001), our data suggest that in the context of courtship conditioning, working memory, STM, and LTM all reside in the same γ5 compartment.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the integration of all experimental results.

claim: Other MB neurons may be involved in courtship memory.
source: Our conclusions do not preclude however, the involvement of other MB neurons in courtship memory (Montague and Baker, 2016) as it is conceivable that modulation, potentially of the opposite sign, of the appetitive memory pathways could be critical for courtship learning (Perisse et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Montague and Baker, 2016 and Perisse et al., 2016.

claim: Modulation of the appetitive memory pathways could be critical for courtship learning.
source: Our conclusions do not preclude however, the involvement of other MB neurons in courtship memory (Montague and Baker, 2016) as it is conceivable that modulation, potentially of the opposite sign, of the appetitive memory pathways could be critical for courtship learning (Perisse et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Perisse et al., 2016.

claim: Distinct courtship memory types are not located in distinct circuits, but rather mediated by distinct processes within a common circuit.
source: We therefore envision that distinct courtship memory types are not located in distinct circuits, but rather mediated by distinct processes within a common circuit.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the integration of all experimental results.

claim: Encoding distinct memory phases within a common circuit may be an efficient mechanism for encoding memories for which the behavioral consequence is largely independent of timing and context.
source: Encoding distinct memory phases within a common circuit may be an efficient mechanism for encoding memories for which the behavioral consequence is largely independent of timing and context (Fusi et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by a citation to Fusi et al., 2005.

claim: SFOCatCh is a step-function channelrhopodsin variant that combines mutations to increase the off kinetics with a single amino acid substitution to enhance the conductance of divalent cations.
source: We generated a step-function channelrhopodsin variant, SFOCatCh, that combines mutations to increase the off kinetics (SFO = C128S/D156A, [Yizhar et al., 2011]) with a single amino acid substitution to enhance the conductance of divalent cations (CatCh = L132C, [Kleinlogel et al., 2011]).
evidence: This is a description of the tool generated for this study, with citation support.

claim: The SFO mutations (C128S/D156A) increase the off kinetics of channelrhodopsin.
source: We generated a step-function channelrhopodsin variant, SFOCatCh, that combines mutations to increase the off kinetics (SFO = C128S/D156A, [Yizhar et al., 2011]) with a single amino acid substitution to enhance the conductance of divalent cations (CatCh = L132C, [Kleinlogel et al., 2011]).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yizhar et al., 2011.

claim: The CatCh mutation (L132C) enhances the conductance of divalent cations in channelrhodopsin.
source: We generated a step-function channelrhopodsin variant, SFOCatCh, that combines mutations to increase the off kinetics (SFO = C128S/D156A, [Yizhar et al., 2011]) with a single amino acid substitution to enhance the conductance of divalent cations (CatCh = L132C, [Kleinlogel et al., 2011]).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kleinlogel et al., 2011.

claim: The combination of SFOCatCh and GCaMP6s temporally uncouples the optical inputs required for activity manipulation and calcium imaging.
source: We used SFOCatCh in conjunction with GCaMP6s (Chen et al., 2013) to monitor calcium responses in whole explanted brains of naïve males. The combination of SFOCatCh and GCaMP6s temporally uncouples the optical inputs required for activity manipulation and calcium imaging.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: We could not detect any robust calcium response in M6 dendrites when we activated MBγ with SFOCatCh in the absence of exogenous dopamine.
source: We could not detect any robust calcium response in either the dendrites (Figure 2B–D) or axon termini (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) of M6 when we activated MBγ with SFOCatCh in the absence of exogenous dopamine.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B-D.

claim: We could not detect any robust calcium response in M6 axon termini when we activated MBγ with SFOCatCh in the absence of exogenous dopamine.
source: We could not detect any robust calcium response in either the dendrites (Figure 2B–D) or axon termini (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) of M6 when we activated MBγ with SFOCatCh in the absence of exogenous dopamine.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The initial stimuli in trials without exogenous dopamine did not elicit a detectable GCaMP6s response in M6 neurons.
source: The initial stimuli, as previously observed in the trials without exogenous dopamine, did not elicit a detectable GCaMP6s response in M6 neurons.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: The prolonged M6 response to repetitive MBγ activation is blocked by AP-5.
source: We could confirm, however, that this prolonged M6 response is blocked by AP-5 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), which inhibits NMDA-type glutamate receptors and the persistent response of aSP13 (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.
